item.title: Seto Inland Sea Island Cruise: Sailing Between the Islands — Guide
item.description: The Seto Inland Sea, the sheltered water between Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu, is one of Japan’s most beautiful landscapes and was its first designated national park. Strewn with hundreds of green, steeply rising islands and famously calm, it has been a highway for a thousand years, and the best way to appreciate it is simply to get on a boat. Options range from local ferries linking island ports for a few hundred yen, to sightseeing cruises from Hiroshima and Onomichi, to overnight luxury cruise ships.

item.title: Shimanami Kaido Cycling: Island-Hopping by Bike — Guide
item.description: The Shimanami Kaido is the finest cycling route in Japan and one of the best anywhere: a roughly 70-kilometre course running from Onomichi in Hiroshima across six islands of the Seto Inland Sea to Imabari in Shikoku. Uniquely, every bridge on the route carries a dedicated, separated cycle lane with gentle spiral approach ramps, so riders cross high above the sea in complete safety. Between the bridges the route rolls through fishing villages, citrus groves and quiet island roads, with a blue line painted on the tarmac guiding you the whole way.

item.title: Shimanami Kaido: The Complete Cycling Guide from Imabari to Onomichi
item.description: The Shimanami Kaido connects Imabari in Ehime to Onomichi in Hiroshima Prefecture across 70 kilometres of bridges and islands spanning the Seto Inland Sea. It is widely regarded as the world’s most scenic cycling route, and it earns that description not through superlative natural spectacle but through something quieter: a sustained sense of moving through island light over calm blue-grey water, with small fishing ports and citrus-scented hillsides at every stop.
